s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic pruritic skin condition with erythematous papules and lymphoid infiltrate
salient_findings: Erythematous papules with crusts and excoriations on trunk and upper extremities
Scales and fissures on lower lip with sparing of surrounding skin
key_facts: Female patient in her early 40s
No other medical history
Topical corticosteroids ineffective
Erythematous papules and excoriations on physical examination
Scales and fissures on lower lip
Normal blood test results including antinuclear antibodies and complement
Normal urine porphyrin analysis
Skin biopsy showed spongiosis and erosions in epidermis
Nodular lymphocyte infiltrate in upper and mid dermis
CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative cells in germinal center
Delayed erythema after UV-A irradiation

shortlist.label: Cutaneous B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Nodular lymphocyte infiltrate in the dermis with CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative cells

shortlist.label: Primary cutaneous follicle center lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Germinal center formation in the dermis with CD20 positive cells

shortlist.label: Pityriasis lichenoides chronica
shortlist.why_kept: Erythematous papules and scales on the skin, consistent with chronic pruritic skin condition

shortlist.label: Lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Erythematous papules and excoriations on physical examination, consistent with chronic pruritic skin condition

shortlist.label: Polymorphic light eruption
shortlist.why_kept: Delayed erythema after UV-A irradiation, consistent with photosensitive reaction

raw.rationale: The presence of a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate in the upper and mid dermis with a peripheral mantle zone surrounding a central germinal center, along with CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative cells, strongly supports the diagnosis of cutaneous B-cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Primary cutaneous follicle center lymphoma
rejected.why: While similar, the specific characteristics of the lymphoid infiltrate and the presence of CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative cells are more indicative of a general cutaneous B-cell lymphoma rather than a specific follicle center type.

rejected.label: Pityriasis lichenoides chronica
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and histopathological findings do not align with the typical features of pityriasis lichenoides chronica, which usually shows a more superficial infiltrate and lacks the distinct germinal centers.

rejected.label: Lichen planus
rejected.why: The absence of basal cell degeneration, colloid bodies, and the specific pattern of lymphocyte infiltration do not support lichen planus as the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Polymorphic light eruption
rejected.why: While the patient exhibits a delayed erythema after UV-A irradiation, the overall clinical and histological picture does not fit the typical presentation of polymorphic light eruption, which usually lacks the deep nodular lymphoid infiltrates and specific immunophenotypic markers found in this case.
